candidate_reports.remark: Received public report of a measured 7.19" rainfall amount south of Jefferson SC.
Public weather station recorded 5.84 inches of rain between 6p and 945p.
Burke County Dispatch reports road flooding at intersection of GA 56 and Byne Sunshine Rd.

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in west central Burke County. A tornado touched down in the swampland south of Highway 80 near rocky Creek. It moved northeast across Highway 80 and Abrams Rd_ turning north and crossing Forest Hill Rd before lifting. Significant damage occurred at a residential farmstead on Hwy 80_ including roof damage_ multiple large trees uprooted_ toppled portions of a center-pivot irrigation system_ and multiple 18-wheeler trailers toppled over. The rest of the damage was mainly trees and limbs.
Numerous reports with video and drone footage of several destroyed homes_ flipped farm equipment_ and considerable tree-powerline damage along highway 80 west of Waynesboro.

NWS storm survey team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in southern Barnwell County. A tornado developed south of Boiling Springs Rd_ east of Shepherd Rd._ moved to the north across a large heavily wooded field_ before dissipating near Poplar Road. The tornado snapped numerous hardwood trees.
Storm spotters showed video of tornado on the ground west of Kline. Radar confirmed debris as well.

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in Barnwell County. A tornado developed along Hwy 278 south of Mount Olive Cir_ then continued north into the City of Barnwell_ before turning northwest through Long Branch and dissipating just north of downtown Williston. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage along its path_ with the most intense damage occurring in a wooded area along a field south of Freedom Road where numerous large hardwood trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado lifted on the north side of Williston near Wilton Drive.
Storm spotters showed video of tornado on the ground near highway 37. Radar confirmed debris as well.
Burke County EM reports the road is washed out near the intersection of Keysville Boggs Academy Rd and Taylor Rd.
Storm Spotters reported tornado northwest on Barnwell along 278. Radar confirmed debris as well.
Personal rain guage from reporting a total accumulation of 4.46 inches. 2 inches of rain fell between 4:09 PM and 4:39 PM in 30 minutes.

Aiken County EM relayed a report of two downed trees. One near the interaction of Coleman Bridge Road and Quail Run Road_ the other near the intersection of Coleman Bridge Road and Bethcar Church Road. Time estimated by radar.

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in northern Aiken County. A tornado touched down just southeast of Bethcar Church Rd. It quickly strengthened and moved northwestward_ causing mostly tree damage along its path. The most significant damage was noted beginning alone Coleman Bridge Rd and continuing along Quail Run Rd where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. The tornado continued causing damage as it moved northwestward_ crossing Kennedy Dr and Camp Rawls Rd with sporadic tree damage noted. The tornado likely lifted in a swampy area north of Eagerton Rd where the final snapped/uprooted trees were noted.
Trained spotter reported water over the road to the top of the vehicle tires and the water was approaching homes along Hwy 1.
Personal weather station measured 4.4 inches with 2 inches falling within 40 min.
Report via social media of Hwy 178 flooded at the bottom of the hill near Moores Creek.
Saluda dispatch reported roadway flooding with water over the road on Ridge Spring hwy near Peters Creek.
Saluda dispatch reported flooded roadways with water covering the road on Denny hwy near Philippi Church Rd.
Personal weather station measured 4.18 inches of rain with 2 inches falling within 45 minutes.
Personal weather station measured 4.19 inches of rain with 2 inches falling within 40 min.

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-2 tornado in northeastern Newberry County. The tornado touched down near or just before the intersection of Old Blair Road and Henderson Ferry Road where it snapped branches of multiple pine trees and uprooted or snapped several other pines. The tornado crossed the clearing and followed Old Blair Road_ snapping and uprooting various hardwood and softwood trees. A home located off of Old Blair Road had several large pine trees snapped or uprooted around the property. There was a small camper on the property which was flipped. As the tornado continued northeastward towards the Broad River it reached the maximum intensity with peak winds estimated to be 115 mph. Much of the forested area along Old Blair Road was destroyed with numerous snapped pine trees found along and north of the road. The trees also brought down several power poles after falling on the poles or attached lines. The tornado lifted just before reaching the Broad River.
Newberry dispatch reported trees down along Old Blair Road. KCAE confirmed debris signature at this time and location.
